title: Hand a half-finished task from one agent to another
summary: A developer added a one-word 'checkpoint' command to his agent tool; he says Claude Opus resumed a task a local Qwen model had stalled on and finished it.
agent_role: On 'checkpoint' the agent packages what is done, what is next and where files live; on 'resume' another agent loads it and continues. The human decides when to stop and switch.
outcome: Author reports Claude picked up the stalled task and finished it without further prompting.
what_they_did: A developer runs local AI models on his Dell. Long tasks slowed them down and filled their memory. He added a 'checkpoint' command to his own agent tool, Valet. The agent saves a summary of progress, next steps and file locations. Saying 'resume' in any new session or agent loads it.
how_it_went: He says a local model struggled with a hard coding task, so he made a checkpoint. He then asked Claude Opus to resume, and he reports it finished the task without more prompting.
worth_knowing: Old checkpoints archive themselves when resumed or replaced, so stale handoff notes do not pile up.
prompt: When I say "checkpoint", write a handoff note to [file path, e.g. CHECKPOINT.md] covering: the goal, what is done, what is left, key decisions, and where the relevant files live. Move any older checkpoint to an archive folder. When I say "resume" in a new session, read the latest checkpoint, summarize your understanding and next step, and wait for my go-ahead before continuing on [project].

curation.rationale: A real handoff between a local model and Claude that finished a task, but it is a single anecdote about the author's own tool with no code or numbers.
